t: NYC Comptroller to propose $5 billion in new private-markets climate investments
s: NYC Comptroller Mark Levine plans to bring $5 billion of private-market climate deals to the NYCERS, TRS and BERS pension boards, spanning renewables, grids and building decarbonization. The ~$300 billion city pensions target $37.8 billion in climate investments by 2035 and net zero by 2040.

t: J.P. Morgan Natural Capital and Paraguay launch $200 million sustainable forestry platform
s: J.P. Morgan Natural Capital is partnering with Paraguay's Office of the President and local group Grupo Robinson on a roughly $200 million forestry platform combining commercial plantations, native forest restoration, timber and carbon credits. Deployment is due to start in early 2027, reflecting nature's rise as an institutional asset class.

t: Crédit Agricole launches natural capital division; Amundi targets €200 million forest restoration fund
s: Crédit Agricole set up a Natural Capital division, Crédit Agricole Capital Naturel, headed by Timothée Jaulin and first focused on European forests. Its asset manager Amundi launched Amundi Arbora Nova, aiming to raise €200 million over time for forest restoration, and the group is in exclusive talks to buy a majority of EcoTree.

t: Achmea and ILX team up on an emerging-markets debt impact platform for Dutch pensions
s: Achmea Investment Management and ILX Management are building an emerging-markets debt impact vehicle for Dutch pension funds, mainly holding loans originated by multilateral development banks and DFIs with explicit impact goals in climate, biodiversity, health and equality. Size was not disclosed; it is a model for linking public and private capital.

t: Actis launches Leo Energies, its fourth Indian clean energy platform, targeting over 3GW
s: General Atlantic-owned Actis launched Leo Energies in India, aiming for a portfolio of over 3GW of wind, solar and storage. It has agreed to buy about 650MWp of operating solar across five states under long-term PPAs, marking Actis's fourth Indian renewables platform built through a buy-and-build approach.

t: TPG raises $10 billion for its second climate private equity fund
s: TPG has raised $10 billion for TPG Rise Climate II, which was due to close to new money at end-September, Bloomberg reported. UAE-backed Alterra committed around $1 billion. The Rise Climate platform had $17.1 billion in total commitments as of August, a sign large LPs still back the energy transition.

t: UK FCA drops mandatory IFRS-based climate reporting in favour of comply-or-explain
s: The FCA scrapped plans to make climate disclosures mandatory for UK listed companies, applying comply-or-explain to all UK SRS S1 and S2 requirements while keeping Scope 3 relief. Rules cover periods from 1 January 2027, with first reports in 2028, which may leave investors with patchier climate data.

t: Vietnam becomes GSG Impact's 44th National Partner and 13th in Asia Pacific
s: Vietnam Impact Alliance became GSG Impact's 44th National Partner and the 13th in Asia Pacific, taking the GSG Impact Partnership to 49 countries. It will convene government, investors, business and civil society to build Vietnam's impact economy as the country seeks capital for its climate transition and inclusive growth.

t: Reverion raises $175 million Series B for carbon-negative-capable power plants
s: German fuel-cell startup Reverion raised a $175 million Series B led by Kembara, joined by Energy Impact Partners, Aurum Impact and Carbon Equity among others. Its plants reach 74.2% electrical efficiency and can deliver negative emissions with biogas and carbon storage; it plans a tenfold capacity jump to 250 MW.

t: Armadin, Kevin Mandia's agentic security startup, raises $255.5M Series B at $2.5B+ valuation
s: Armadin closed a $255.5M Series B co-led by a16z and Accel, valuing it above $2.5B and lifting total funding to $445M, roughly seven months after leaving stealth. Investors are betting heavily on AI agents that probe enterprise defenses like attackers.

t: EliseAI raises $350M at a $4B valuation
s: EliseAI raised $350M led by a16z and Bessemer at a $4B valuation, after passing $200M in annual recurring revenue in June and doubling revenue for five straight years. It shows vertical AI apps can now justify unicorn-plus prices with real revenue.

t: Protego Ventures closes debut $125M fund for Israeli defense tech
s: Protego Ventures, founded by Lital Leshem and Lee Moser, completed its $125M Fund I ($70M at first closing plus $55M) to back battle-tested Israeli defense startups. Portfolio firm XTEND listed on the NYSE at a $1.5B valuation; Fund II will lean into the US.

t: India's Q3 startup funding edges up 5% to $2.2B as investors get selective
s: Indian startups raised $2.2B in Q3 2026, up 5% YoY, while deal count fell 13% to 210, per Inc42. Four $100M+ rounds and a 38% jump in Series A–B money drove growth; AI funding hit $438M, up 265%, as capital concentrates in fewer bets.

t: Korea's VC investment tops ₩10 trillion in nine months, a four-year high
s: VC investment in South Korean startups reached ₩10 trillion ($7.4B) in the first nine months, crossing that mark for the first time since the 2022 boom. AI chips, biotech and healthcare (about ₩2 trillion) and robotics led, and average deal size more than doubled.

t: Korea Venture Investment launches first fund of funds using corporate partnership money
s: Korea Venture Investment Corp. formed a fund of funds on Sept 30 using ₩3B that KB Financial Group put into a large-small business cooperation fund, aiming for at least ₩5B in sub-funds for impact companies. A revised enforcement decree now lets such corporate money flow into VC partnerships.

t: HarbourVest reportedly buys GIC's $1B private fund portfolio in secondary deal
s: HarbourVest is reported to be acquiring a $1B portfolio of private fund stakes from Singapore sovereign fund GIC in a secondary transaction, giving it a diversified pool of fund interests. Large Asian LPs are increasingly using secondaries to rebalance private-market exposure.

t: Firmus prices $5B IPO as valuation nearly triples in two months, splitting investors
s: Blackstone- and Nvidia-backed Australian data-centre operator Firmus priced its $5B IPO at A$11 a share, for a $30.6B equity valuation, nearly triple its $10.5B mark in early August. It lists on the ASX on Oct 23, but ~$30B of debt and execution risk worry some fund managers.

t: Europe's Q3 VC fundraising: Index, Highland and Accel lead 21 new funds
s: Vestbee tallied 21 new European and CEE VC funds in Q3: Index Ventures raised $2B (its growth vehicle now $2.2B), Highland Europe €1.1B for Fund VI and Accel $800M for its ninth European fund. AI is the common thread, while defence and dual-use capital keeps growing, with Airbus among new LPs.

t: Taiwan-based GMI Cloud closes $223M Series B plus $440M credit facility
s: GMI Cloud, a Taiwan-based GPU cloud provider, closed a $223M Series B led by ARCHIV with Nvidia and Trend Micro participating, plus a $440M credit facility from ChinaTrust, about $663M in total. Funds will expand data centres globally and its sovereign AI push in Japan — a rare mega-raise for a Taiwanese infrastructure startup.

t: Security startup TRAPA wins investment from Japan's GMO group to enter Japan
s: Taiwanese cybersecurity startup TRAPA received a strategic investment from GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae, part of listed GMO Internet Group, which gains exclusive Japan rights to its TRAPA CYBER RANGE drill platform. Serving 100+ large enterprises at home, TRAPA makes Japan its first overseas market.

t: NextDrive tops Japan's HEMS gateway market as it advances toward a TSE IPO
s: Taiwanese energy-IoT startup NextDrive holds 42.9% of Japan's HEMS gateway market, well ahead of the runner-up at 25.7%. Picked for the TSE Asia Startup Hub three years running, it has over 62 financial institutions mobilised to support a Tokyo listing — a bellwether for Taiwanese startups eyeing Japan IPOs.

t: MODA's NT$10B AI startup investment plan opens to offshore firms operating mainly in Taiwan
s: Taiwan's digital ministry widened its NT$10B AI startup co-investment plan to offshore companies with at least 50% of R&D, revenue or staff in Taiwan. By August it had backed 10 firms with about NT$255M from the National Development Fund, drawing some NT$570M in private money — a bid to keep Taiwanese AI teams with overseas holding structures in reach.

t: Four Taiwanese startups named to Forbes Asia's 100 to Watch list
s: Four Taiwanese startups made the 6th Forbes Asia 100 to Watch list: Syncell, KopherBit, Ohmplus Technology and AimFolds, spanning medtech, EV control systems and RF testing. Syncell closed a $20M Series A extension in July and KopherBit a $4.3M pre-A early this year, signalling regional recognition of Taiwan's deep tech.

t: Edge-AI inspection startup Overview projects $30M revenue, moves R&D back to Taiwan
s: Overview, a US-registered edge-AI visual inspection company co-founded with a Taiwanese founder, projects 2026 revenue of $30M, tripling year on year, and in August moved its R&D team to Taiwan, now 40+ staff there. It earlier raised about $13M across Series A and bridge rounds.

t: Y Combinator's Startup School comes to Taipei on Nov 12
s: Y Combinator will hold a free Startup School in Taipei on November 12, with four YC alumni speakers including founders from DoorDash and Xendit, covering MVPs, growth and fundraising. Its application stresses shipped work and founders' networks, a sign of YC's growing interest in Taiwanese founders.

t: TWSE teams up with AAMA to coach startups on Taiwan Innovation Board IPOs
s: The Taiwan Stock Exchange and AAMA held a session on moving from IPO preparation to investor communication, drawing 17 companies and about 23 representatives from AI, biotech and cloud. A founder whose company listed on the Taiwan Innovation Board on Sept 22 shared lessons, as TWSE works to build the board's listing pipeline.

t: Asia's EAMs turn into tech platforms, chasing B2B SaaS revenue
s: Asia's external asset managers (EAMs) are entering a new phase of competition, building proprietary tech platforms and offering them to others in a bid to earn B2B SaaS revenue and win market share — a shift from pure advisory toward wealth-tech services that could change how family offices pick providers.

t: StanChart: philanthropy is 'training wheels' for family governance
s: Scott Chang, Asia philanthropy head at Standard Chartered Global Private Bank, says structured giving acts as 'training wheels' for family governance and succession, helping families align before discussing wealth transfer, and argues philanthropy should not be sold as a product.

t: Family offices now outsize the global VC industry
s: Single-family offices oversee about $5.5 trillion (Citi Wealth puts it at $5.9-6.9 trillion), above the $1-1.5 trillion venture industry. Their number has grown over 75% since 2020 to more than 10,700, and 70% make direct investments, competing with PE and VC for deals.

t: Taiwan Trust Association pushes succession trusts as elderly-care trusts top NT$207.5bn
s: Taiwan's Trust Association held a succession-trust briefing on Sept 24 with Mega Bank and Cathay United Bank. As of June 2026, elderly-care trusts had over 227,000 beneficiaries and more than NT$207.5 billion entrusted; with Taiwan super-aged since end-2025, equity succession trusts are drawing demand.

t: After $29.1bn sale, Kirsh family builds out New York family office
s: After agreeing to sell Jetro Restaurant Depot to Sysco for $29.1 billion including debt ($21.6 billion cash plus 91.5 million Sysco shares), 94-year-old billionaire Natie Kirsh's family is expanding its New York office, recruiting a CIO, investment committee members and heads of public and private investments.

t: Family offices made fewer bets in September but backed big rounds
s: Family offices logged 42 direct company investments in September, down from 52 in August, per Fintrx data shared with CNBC, but backed large rounds: Hillspire joined Mistral's roughly $3.4 billion Series D, Duquesne backed Fab2 and Precision Neuroscience, and Mazama Energy raised a $135 million Series B.

t: Barclays Private Bank: 72% of wealthy investors now in private markets
s: A Barclays Private Bank survey of 600-plus wealthy investors in the UK, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and Africa found 72% now invest in private markets (50% in 2025) and 60% plan to add more, though average allocations slipped from 30% to 27%; 41% want shorter lock-ups.

t: Taiwan Cabinet reaches consensus on successive-beneficiary trusts
s: Trust Association secretary-general Lin Chih-chi writes that a Cabinet inter-ministry review has reached consensus on the duration and tax principles of 'successive-beneficiary trusts', letting families pair securities trusts with control and succession; he notes $83 trillion will change generations globally within 20-30 years.

t: As the US retreats, Asia's investors take the lead on climate financing
s: Asian asset owners including Temasek and the Tsao Family Office say regional climate investing is pressing ahead; the Asia Ocean Fund targets $75M across 30 Asia-Pacific deals.

t: Gender-lens investors look to scale capital in public markets
s: At 2X Global's Montreal summit (270 participants from 44 countries), investors pushed to extend gender-lens strategies into public equities and debt, targeting $20B in new capital by 2027; FinDev Canada committed C$30M.

t: GIIN's Amit Bouri reflects as he steps down after 17 years
s: Bouri, who led the GIIN for 17 years, steps down after the October Amsterdam forum; the market grew from about $500B (2019) to $1.5T, yet he says systemic progress remains insufficient.

t: Climate Week NYC: McKnight backs a $150M fund for community-owned climate projects
s: McKnight Foundation mapped 110+ community-owned climate projects across seven Midwest states (about $450M in total cost) and helped launch the $150M Power & Place fund to close the gap, even as climate-specialist VC fundraising slows.

t: Japan's ¥18.65 trillion impact market anchors first Impact Galleria Tokyo, linking 10 Asian ecosystems
s: Japan's outstanding impact investments reached about ¥18.65 trillion (~$125bn), and the first Impact Galleria Tokyo drew some 300 participants from 10 countries. AVPN noted Asia's real bottleneck is bankable deals, not capital.

t: 500 development banks to meet in Bangkok as Finance in Common Summit comes to Asia for the first time
s: ADB will host the Finance in Common Summit in Bangkok from 31 March to 2 April 2027, the first in Asia, gathering 500+ public development banks managing roughly $23trn and investing about $2.5trn a year—raising Asia's profile as a hub for mobilising private capital.

t: EU greenwashing rules take effect: net-zero claims need verified plans, offset-based 'carbon neutral' labels banned
s: The EU's EmpCo Directive now applies: net-zero pledges need measurable, time-bound plans with independent verification, and offset-reliant products can no longer be labelled 'carbon neutral'. Banks are covered too, though at least 17 member states had not transposed it as of June.

t: Enable Ventures raises $50.3 million for disability-tech venture fund
s: Disability-lens VC Enable Ventures closed its fund at $50.3m (vs a $75m target), backed by the Ford Foundation, UnitedHealth Group and others. It has made 11 investments and plans about 24, signalling disability as an emerging impact theme.

t: Bessemer Venture Partners closes $5.75B for AI-native founders
s: The raise splits into $1.75B for seed/early stage and $4B for growth, targeting AI-native companies from infrastructure and models to apps and agents.

t: The week's 10 biggest rounds: Island and Cyera lead with $400M each
s: Island ($6.4B valuation) and Cyera each raised $400M, while Snorkel AI raised $350M at $3.2B; security, AI and health dominated the week's megadeals.

t: Jumbo-sized Series A rounds are on the rise
s: At least 114 Series A rounds of $100M+ have closed globally in 2026, totaling roughly $33B and on pace for a record; over 70% went to AI startups.

t: OpenAI reportedly in talks to raise $30B round at $1.4T valuation
s: OpenAI is reportedly negotiating a round of at least $30B at roughly a $1.4T valuation, up from $852B in March, underscoring how heavily capital is concentrating in frontier AI ahead of its expected listing next year.

t: Viral AI agent Instinct raises $1B Series C at a $10B valuation
s: Consumer AI agent Instinct, which books travel, pays bills and shops for users, raised a $1B Series C from Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue at a $10B valuation, about a month after a round at $2.5B, showing how fast capital is chasing AI agents.

t: Ahead of US IPO, British AI neocloud Nscale secures $3.36B in convertible financing
s: Nvidia-backed British AI cloud provider Nscale lined up $3.36B in convertible notes led by Third Point and Nvidia ahead of an NYSE listing expected to value it around $35B, illustrating the scale of capital needed for AI data center buildouts.

t: GCash owner Mynt prices Philippine IPO at 6.6 pesos per share
s: Mynt, parent of Philippine e-wallet GCash, priced its IPO at 6.60 pesos a share to raise about 53B pesos (~$845M), with trading set for Oct. 20 and cornerstones including Capital Research and the IFC, a bellwether exit for Southeast Asian fintech.

t: SE Asia venture capital grapples with structural gap in follow-on funding
s: Southeast Asian startups raised $7.25B in H1 2026, but $4.5B came from DayOne's single Series C; excluding it, funding fell 21% to $2.75B and median Series A size dropped to $8M, exposing a structural gap in growth-stage capital.

t: Lightspeed targets $250M for new India fund, focusing on early-stage AI
s: Lightspeed is raising $250M for its fifth India fund, with 80% already committed, to back early-stage AI startups in India and Southeast Asia; the fund is half the size of its $500M 2022 predecessor, signaling a leaner, more selective approach.

t: FunNow raises $10M Series C from Hotai Motor, targeting Japan
s: Instant-booking platform FunNow closed a ~NT$318M Series C from Hotai Motor, integrating with Hotai's chicTrip travel platform to expand into Japan and invest in AI; it entered IPO counseling in July.

t: Standard Chartered Women Entrepreneurship Award names its fourth-cohort winners
s: Co-run by Standard Chartered, the Lih Jen Foundation and Impact Hub Taipei, the award's top three were an elder meal-delivery platform, a service-dog team and an AI fit-tech brand; nearly 120 women-led teams have been trained since 2023.

t: LANDED's 12-month program helps Taiwanese startups land in the US
s: Founded by New York-based Taiwanese entrepreneur Huang Sheng-an, LANDED runs a three-phase program (validation, revenue, fundraising) and has backed nine startups since 2025, including YC S26 insurtech Qlo.

t: Taiwan Startup Investment Hit US$2.774B in 2025 as AI and Chips Set Records
s: MOEA's SME and startup agency reported 555 deals worth US$2.774B in 2025, with AI startups raising US$569M (up ~80%) and semiconductors US$442M (up 70%+), showing capital concentrating in AI and chips.

t: iReach Raises NT$340M for AI Optical Interconnect, with National Development Fund Joining
s: VCSEL maker iReach closed a NT$340M round led by Da-Ying, joined by the National Development Fund and optical-comms strategic investors, to expand R&D and testing for AI chip-to-chip optical interconnects, targeting small-volume output in 2027-28.

t: TMYTEK Debuts on Taiwan Innovation Board, Gains Over 16% on First Day
s: Millimeter-wave startup TMYTEK (7812) moved from the emerging market to the Taiwan Innovation Board on Sept 22, closing at NT$70 versus a NT$60 offer price, a 16%+ gain and a marker for satellite and defense startups reaching public markets.

t: FSC-NDC TiBOOST Program for AI Startups Extends Application Deadline to Oct 5
s: The TiBOOST program, backed by the FSC and NDC and run by TWSE, drew 100+ applications by Sept 29, about half from 19 countries abroad, and extended its deadline to Oct 5 to link AI startups with capital and industry partners.

t: Foxconn Chairman Young Liu Lays Out Five Criteria for Startup Investing
s: Young Liu said Foxconn screens startups on timing, execution, synergy, explainability and exit planning; since 2019 its direct strategic bets show 20 successes out of 33, while its five funds count 321 out of 594, under a three-year review rule.

t: NDC Opens First Overseas Talent Office in Silicon Valley, 12 Startups Pitch at Taiwan Demo Day
s: The NDC opened Talent Taiwan's first overseas office inside its Startup Island TAIWAN Silicon Valley hub; a parallel Career Day drew 3,000+ attendees and 14 Taiwanese firms, while 12 startups pitched at Taiwan Demo Day.

t: Citi: Asia-Pacific family offices lead in direct investing and AI
s: Citi's 2026 survey found 79% of APAC family offices invest directly and 80% name AI a primary sector focus, both the highest globally; 26% report YTD returns above 15%.

t: TMF Group: family offices rethink how they choose jurisdictions
s: Only 31% of family offices pick a jurisdiction mainly for proximity to assets, with political and economic stability at 23% each; most now add jurisdictions rather than relocate, with Singapore and Hong Kong as key hubs.

t: Carlyle hires two executives to lead its family office business
s: Carlyle named David Seeberan global head of its family office group and ex-BlackRock Victoria Matthews to lead Europe and Asia, supporting its goal of raising $200B+ from private wealth by 2028.

t: RBC–Campden North America Family Office Report flags liquidity squeeze and pay gap
s: RBC and Campden Wealth's survey of 155 North American family offices found nearly half of private-fund investors could not exit as planned, while non-family CEOs earn $721,000 versus $460,000 for family CEOs, putting liquidity and talent pricing at the center of family office governance.

t: MAS SFO framework tilts field to private banks, pushing EAMs to sub-S$20m market, says MFO chief
s: The CEO of Rockstead Capital, a multi-family office with about US$1.4bn in assets, said requirements in MAS's streamlined single-family office framework favour private banks and could push boutique external asset managers toward families with under S$20m.

t: Family succession services become Taiwan state-run banks' next battleground
s: With AI supply-chain wealth swelling, Taiwan's state-run banks are chasing ultra-wealthy clients; Mega Bank's high-net-worth clients rose 19% to 2,232 with AUM above NT$264bn (+25%), as it builds around investment, financing and succession.

t: Northwestern Mutual launches Family Office Services for $50m-plus clients
s: Northwestern Mutual rolled out Family Office Services combining legal, tax, investment, philanthropy and legacy planning for clients worth at least $50m, backed by 40-plus in-house specialists, as large firms productise family office capabilities.

t: Wealth Enhancement to acquire RWA Wealth Partners, bolstering UHNW family office offering
s: Wealth Enhancement agreed to buy Boston-based RWA Wealth Partners, with about $22.46bn in client assets, lifting combined assets above $187.1bn and adding trust, estate and family governance expertise for its $25m-plus client tier.

t: Americana Partners launches multi-family office business
s: Americana Partners, with $12.1bn in assets, launched a multi-family office unit led by Matt Celenza, folding in accounting capabilities from its 2026 NRT Consulting acquisition to serve US and Latin American UHNW families needing coordinated multigenerational planning.
